entities.summary: Nicholas Hawksmoor was an English architect. He was a leading figure of the English Baroque style of architecture in the late-seventeenth and early-eighteenth centuries. Hawksmoor worked alongside the principal architects of the time, Christopher Wren and John Vanbrugh, and contributed to the design of some of the most notable buildings of the period, including St Paul's Cathedral, Wren's City of London churches, Greenwich Hospital, Blenheim Palace and Castle Howard. Part of his work has been correctly attributed to him only relatively recently, and his influence has reached several poets and authors of the twentieth century.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Hawksmoor's contributions to English Baroque architecture had a significant regional impact, influencing the design of prominent buildings in England and shaping the country's architectural identity. His work also had an enduring influence on poets and authors of the twentieth century.
